> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `ObjectQL (symbol, 72 pages)`, `VALIDATION_FAILED (literal, 35 pages)`
- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **55** of **207** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **38** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 785a7c3b3e31a669ef52e0d83bc18916d170ae9c` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `fd8fc59514bcfaca6d079a3fbaf9c1185e3a22d3` — the merge of head `80b0a99e12f72ea46d99072cfd3820ee2d04b03b` into base `785a7c3b3e31a669ef52e0d83bc18916d170ae9c`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin fd8fc59514bcfaca6d079a3fbaf9c1185e3a22d3 && git checkout fd8fc59514bcfaca6d079a3fbaf9c1185e3a22d3
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 785a7c3b3e31a669ef52e0d83bc18916d170ae9c 80b0a99e12f72ea46d99072cfd3820ee2d04b03b && git checkout -B drift-repro 785a7c3b3e31a669ef52e0d83bc18916d170ae9c && git merge --no-ff 80b0a99e12f72ea46d99072cfd3820ee2d04b03b

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 785a7c3b3e31a669ef52e0d83bc18916d170ae9c
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 785a7c3b3e31a669ef52e0d83bc18916d170ae9c` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `80b0a99e12f72ea46d99072cfd3820ee2d04b03b`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/core/src/utils/import-runner.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine.ts, packages/core/src/utils/import-runner-dry-run-batch.test.ts, packages/core/src/utils/import-runner-dropped-fields.test.ts, packages/core/src/utils/import-runner-kept-options.test.ts, packages/core/src/utils/import-runner-update-preview-address.test.ts, packages/objectql/src/validate-preview-parent.test.ts, packages/rest/src/import-dry-run-batch-parent-summary.test.ts + packages/objectql/src/engine-referential-integrity.ts (`assertReferencesResolve` body), packages/core/src/utils/bulk-write.ts (the commit's chunking), packages/rest/src/data-action-routes.ts (the sync import door and the import job, both callers of `runImport`), packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts (`validateData` forwarding to `engine.validate`), packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts (`ValidateDataResponseSchema`, read only), packages/objectql/src/validation/record-validator.ts (`normalizeMultiValueFields`), packages/core/src/utils/import-coerce.ts (multi-value cell split), content/docs/data-modeling/fields.mdx, content/docs/data-modeling/import-mappings.mdx :176, .changeset/26684-import-dry-run-batch-preview.md, .claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/review-checklist.md :50

Face: narrowing. Card #26684, PR #26778, net diff `origin/main` (`785a7c3b3e`, merge base `1685a06dd9`)...`80b0a99e12`: 10 files, +647/−46. Read-only: the diff, the card body and all six comments (seat addendum `6442401477`, triage `6442590531`, claim `6444444867`, os-dev-report `6445989077`, seat ruling `6446027005`), the PR body and file list, and the head's check-runs, read at 2026-10-27T15:29Z. Rendered by the seat's subagent.

### ① Derived judgments

**D1 — the narrowing at the import dry run (`POST /api/v1/data/:object/import` with `dryRun: true`, and `POST .../import/jobs` with `dryRun: true`): right.** Both doors reach one runner (`data-action-routes.ts` :392 sync, :567 job; the job passes `progressEvery: 200`, the sync door takes the runner's default `Math.max(1, opts.progressEvery ?? 200)` at import-runner.ts :718), so both narrow the same way. On `main` a create-resolved row was asked alone (`previewVerdict(data, 'insert', rowCtx)`, one row object, `results[0]`). At head a create-resolved row is pushed to `pendingPreviews` (:1424) and flushed by `flushPendingPreviews` (:1322-1337) in runs of `Math.min(progressEvery, MAX_CREATE_BATCH_SIZE)` through `previewCreateRun`, which hands the run to `p.validateData` as ONE call with `data` an array in file order. Two requests that answered valid on `main` and are refused at head, each pinned through the real door over a real engine and sqlite (rest test, 9 cases): (a) a create row a batch-aware parent-summary rule refuses once the earlier admitted rows of its batch are counted (two primary contacts for one new supplier; row 2 `ok: false`, `action: 'failed'`, the rule's own message, equal to the commit's verdict row for row); (b) a create row whose caller-supplied reference names no row (`region: 'nowhere'`), refused with the write's `reference_not_found` and not counted toward a later row's summary (the multi-row preview answers `[false, true]` as `insertMany` answers `[false, true]`). Nothing widened: a row the per-row preview refused on `main` is refused at head too (the batch overlay only adds counted rows; a row the rules refuse is not accepted into the accumulator, `batchSummaries?.accept(row)` runs only after the admit step).

**D2 — update-mode previews unchanged: right.** The `willUpdate` arm still calls `previewVerdict({ ...updatePatch(data, matchedKeySet), id: target.id }, 'update', rowCtx)` with one row object (:1419-1421), `previewVerdict` is `previewVerdicts(...)[0] ?? null` (the old `results[0] ?? null`), and `reportPreview(i, rowNo, verdict, target)` is the old inline report lifted verbatim. In the engine the new admit step is gated `mode === 'insert' && mayWrite` (engine.ts :14600), so an `update`-mode `validate()` runs nothing new; the per-row accumulator was already gated on insert mode and more than one row. Pinned: the rest update-mode case (refused against a stored primary, a rename admitted, verdicts equal to the commit) and the core "an update row is asked alone, in update mode" case.

**D3 — the commit path unchanged: right.** The diff touches no line of `flushPendingCreates`, `bulkWrite`'s options, the `willUpdate` write arm, the `canBulkCreate` buffer or the inline `createData` arm; the only new statements on the commit's path are the two `await flushPendingPreviews()` calls (:1478, :1490), which return at once on an empty `pendingPreviews` (a commit never pushes to it: the push sits inside the `else if (dryRun)` arm). In the engine, `insert()` (:14701-15990), `insertMany`, `update()` are untouched; the diff's engine hunks are inside `validate()` only.

**D4 — triage `6442590531`, no second rule copy, same chunking: right.** The runner neither reads nor evaluates a rule: the only engine contact is `p.validateData` (the protocol forwards `request.data` whole to `engine.validate`, protocol.ts :13717-13722), and the accumulation is the engine's `createBatchSummaryAccumulator` already pinned by #26680. Chunking: the preview's run length `Math.min(progressEvery, MAX_CREATE_BATCH_SIZE)` (:1326) is the commit's `batchSize: Math.min(progressEvery, MAX_CREATE_BATCH_SIZE)` (:1187), and `bulkWrite` slices `rows.slice(start, start + batchSize)` in order (bulk-write.ts :217-218) as `flushPendingPreviews` slices `batch.slice(start, start + runLength)`; the checkpoints are the same line (`processed % progressEvery === 0 || processed === rows.length`, :1475) plus the post-loop flush; the buffered population is the same (only create-resolved, coercion-clean, unmatched rows reach either buffer; update rows and refused rows reach neither). The run's context is `writeCtxFor` over the run's rows' `kept` values, the union the commit's `ctxForRows(toCreate)` carries. Pinned by the core test: 450 rows previewed as 200/200/50; `progressEvery: 3` gives `[r1..r3] [r4..r6] [r7]` with progress `3, 6, 7`. The degraded path (a run whose call throws, or answers a verdict count other than one per row) re-asks each row alone and then the survivors together in ONE call again, so even there no accumulation is re-implemented in the runner.

**D5 — the `validate()` admit step vs `insert()`'s: the same method, the same order.** `insert()` (engine.ts :15626-15633): `normalizeMultiValueFields` → `validateRecordInScope(..., 'insert', 'include', ...)` → `evaluateValidationRules(..., related: batchSummaries.overlay(...))` → `await this.assertReferencesResolve(schema, rows[i], suppliedPerRow[i], opCtx.context, msgCtx)` → `batchSummaries?.accept(rows[i])`. `validate()` (:14564-14604): `validateRecordInScope(..., mode, 'include', ...)` → `evaluateValidationRules(..., related: batchSummaries.overlay(...))` → `await this.assertReferencesResolve(schemaForValidation, row, rawRows[i], options?.context, messages)` → `batchSummaries?.accept(row)`. Same private method (one wrapper over `engine-referential-integrity.ts` `assertReferencesResolve`), same position (after the rules, before the accept), same `supplied` meaning (`rawRows[i]` is the caller's payload after the blank/numeric normalizations and the computed strip, before the defaults; `suppliedPerRow[i]` is `callerSuppliedRow` on the caller's keys; the check only uses `supplied` to decide WHETHER a field is checked, by its raw value being non-empty, and reads the value from `data`). The rows are now judged sequentially (`judgeRow` in a `for` loop) so row i's awaited admission precedes row i+1's overlay read; on `main` the `rows.map` callback was synchronous, so the sequential loop preserves order and changes no verdict by itself. One deliberate difference, declared in the PR body and the engine docblock: the preview runs the check only when `mayWrite` (the registered write-gate probe admits the caller); `insert()` has no such gate in the executor because its middleware has already refused the whole write for such a caller. The preview cannot answer the write decision, so withholding the elevated existence probe (and therefore `reference_not_found`) from a refused caller is the honest, fail-closed-on-information direction; pinned ("a caller the write-gate probe refuses is told nothing about which ids exist"). Can it change a single-row preview or a non-batch caller: yes, and it is declared. A single-row `validate()` / `validateData` in `insert` mode now refuses a dangling caller-supplied reference (pinned: "a single-row preview refuses a dangling reference, as the single insert does") and issues one elevated `findOne` per supplied reference id, the read the insert itself makes (pinned in `validate-preview-parent.test.ts`: the insert preview's header reads equal the insert's). The changeset names exactly this: "the insert preview (`validate` / `validateData`, mode `insert`) refuses a row whose caller-supplied reference names no row, which it answered valid before". No REST data route exposes `validateData` directly (`rest-route-ledger.ts` lists only the datasource `external/validate`), so the public reach is the import dry run plus in-process protocol callers; the dev ran the downstream readers it found (plugin-auth admin-import, runtime external-validation, service-datasource, service-automation connector-pull).

**D6 — the per-row verdict shape: unchanged.** `reportPreview` (:1046-1068) is the old inline block moved out of the row loop with the same keys in the same order: `row`, `ok`, `action` (`'failed'` / `'created'` / `'updated'`), `field` when the first error names one, `code` (`first?.code ?? 'VALIDATION_FAILED'`), `error` via the same `composeValidationMessage(verdict.errors)`, `warnings` when present, `droppedFields` via the same `rowDrops`, `id` on an update. `rowNo` (`i + 1`) and `index` travel in the `PendingCreate`, `results[b.index]` is written at the row's own position, and the post-loop `compacted` filter is the old one, so row numbers and order are the file's. The counters (`okCount`, `errCount`, `created`, `updated`) are incremented by the same lines, and the flush runs before `onProgress`, so a checkpoint snapshot carries the same counts it carried when the preview was inline. A row whose preview call throws is reported by the same `toFailedResult(rowNo, err, objectName)` the row loop's `catch` used on `main`. Pinned with `toEqual` on whole result objects in the core test (row 1 `{ row: 1, ok: true, action: 'created' }`, row 2 `{ row: 2, ok: false, action: 'failed', field: 'name', code: 'rule_violation', error: 'refused bad-b' }`).

**D7 — the public surface of `@objectstack/core` and `@objectstack/objectql`: no export, type or signature change.** `runImport`'s options and `ImportRunSummary` are untouched; `ImportProtocolLike.validateData` already took `ValidateDataRequest`, whose `data` admits an array; `ObjectQL.validate`'s signature is unchanged. `packages/spec` untouched (the file list has no spec path; the lane red line holds). `import-mappings.mdx` :176 ("the verdict comes from the engine's own write-path validation") and `export.zod.ts`'s `dryRun` description stay true at head and need no edit.

**D8 — a boundary I read that the PR does not name, judged non-blocking (two observations, both erring toward refusing, neither reachable through the import door):** (i) `previewCreateRun` throws `ERR_BULK_RESULT_MISMATCH` when a responder answers a verdict count other than one per row, and that failure lands on the row (`toFailedResult`) after the per-row degradation; on `main` a responder answering no `results` fell to the coercion verdict (`results?.[0] ?? null`). `ValidateDataResponseSchema.results` is a required array ("one entry per submitted row, in submission order", protocol.zod.ts :2579, :2605), so such a responder violates the contract; the update arm keeps the old tolerance (`verdicts[0] ?? null`). Within contract; noted as an asymmetry, not a defect. (ii) `insert()` runs `normalizeMultiValueFields` before its admit step and the preview never has (pre-existing, outside this diff's hunks), so a `multiple: true` lookup handed to `validateData` as one joined string is probed by the preview as one id where the write splits it first. The import door splits multi-value reference cells in `coerceRow` (import-coerce.ts :789) before the dry run, so dry run and commit agree there; the corner is a direct protocol caller passing a joined string. Named here for the seat; a follow-up card if a caller is found, not a condition on this PR.

### ② Semver level

The changeset `.changeset/26684-import-dry-run-batch-preview.md` bumps `@objectstack/core: patch` and `@objectstack/objectql: patch`, the two packages the diff moves (`packages/rest` carries only a test). Clause-②: `no (narrowing)` on the PR body and in the changeset, line-initial, matching the measured diff: the import dry run and the insert preview refuse requests they admitted (D1, D5), nothing is admitted that was refused, no protocol key moves. Metadata-protocol: `none` — no key, accepted value, metadata type, meaning or default an author can write changes; `packages/spec` is untouched. Per AGENTS.md ("a non-protocol change, widening or breaking, ships `patch` and keeps its BREAKING banner and ADR-0087 disposition"), `patch` is the level; the changeset carries the `fix(core)!:` title, a BREAKING block with Before / Now / Unchanged / Not covered / Who sees it, a remedy, and exactly one ADR-0087 marker, `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`, whose only mechanical condition (no migration prescription in the body) the body meets: nothing is renamed or removed, the refusals are the rule author's own message and the write's existing `reference_not_found`. Check Changeset on the head: `success`. Clause-②: `no (narrowing)` — right.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **os-dev-report `open_questions[0]` (the cross-batch straddle):** answered by seat ruling `6446027005`, letter A, with a condition: the limit must stay stated in `content/docs/data-modeling/fields.mdx` and in the changeset's "Not covered" line. Both are present at head: fields.mdx :325-329 ("It writes nothing, so a row in a later batch reads the summary as stored before the import: two such rows that fall in different batches of a dry run both preview valid, while the import refuses the second"), inside the 批量等于逐条 paragraph where an author reads the rule; the changeset's **Not covered** bullet says the same. The ruling withdrew the order's "agrees across the chunk boundary" pin; the rest test's 203-row case pins agreement for two primaries INSIDE the second batch (rows 201-202), which is what head delivers, and does not claim the straddle. A pin that the limit exists is "welcome, if the PR has one": the PR has none; the ruling makes it optional. Closed.
- **Dev flag — "the update-mode preview does not run the write's reference check (`update()` does)":** out of the addendum's scope (the admit step the addendum names is insert-only), stated in the PR's Acceptance notes and in the engine docblock ("on an insert"); update-mode previews are unchanged (D2). Not a condition; a follow-up card at the seat's discretion. Closed.
- **Dev flag — two update rows that each move a parent summary preview against the stored value:** the ruling keeps update rows per-row, stated in the changeset's "Unchanged" line. Closed.
- **Dev flag — the insert preview now reads one more thing (the reference probe, behind the write-gate probe):** stated in the engine docblock and the PR body; pinned as equal to the insert's own reads. Closed.
- **Dev flag — degraded run costs extra calls only on a failing run:** read in the code (D4); the commit degrades the same way. Closed.
- **Dev flag — open PRs on the touched files (#26337, #26755 on `engine.ts`, #26598 on `fields.mdx`):** #26337 has since merged into `main` (`a9f654ebfb`, in the base range); the PR's `merge-tree` claim is the dev's, and the head's Governed Surface Queue Guard and Lint & Repo Gates are `success`; the Type Check · workspace job is still running at read time, so a conflict with the merged #26337 would surface there. Noted, not a verdict input beyond the check-runs.
- **Seat question — the dogfood battery (review-checklist.md :50: `!` or `(narrowing)` ⇒ the battery pinned to head, full, red fixed or reported):** the report's `dogfood_battery` reads "80b0a99e · os-verify-lock: VERDICT command-exit 0 (held 799s) · Test Files 302 passed | 3 skipped (305) · Tests 2505 passed | 20 skipped (2525) · no failures", and the PR body says no shard, after a dogfood build. `80b0a99e` is this head's short sha; full (no shard); no failures; the skips are declared skips. Met, as the dev's own reading; the head's Dogfood Regression Gate check-run is `success` (its shard matrix skipped on this diff).
- **Seat question — the declarations:** `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` right; `Metadata-protocol: none` right; `patch` with the BREAKING block and the ADR-0087 marker right (section ②). The Skills-docs line names a measured grep; no `skills/**` path is in the diff.
- **D8 (i) and (ii)** are this review's own observations, recorded there; neither conditions the verdict.
- **Stale comment, non-blocking:** import-runner.ts :60 still reads "the dry run: `validateData`'s verdict for the row (`results[0]`)"; at head a create row's verdict is entry k of its run's call. Cosmetic; a one-line follow-up if the seat wants the docblock exact.

| item | reading |
|:--|:--|
| Shape | Draft, base `main`, `Fixes #26684` under triage `6442590531`. 10 files: `import-runner.ts` and four of its tests, `engine.ts` (the multi-row `validate()` admit step) and its test, a REST dry-run test, `fields.mdx`, and a `patch` changeset for `core` and `objectql` with a BREAKING block and ADR-0087 `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`. `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: none` appear in both the body and the changeset. |
